candidates.name: Roy Cooper
candidates.background: Governor of North Carolina 2017–2025; NC Attorney General 2001–2017. Won the March 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

cost.label: 'Make Stuff Cost Less' platform: block grocery mergers, ban algorithmic pricing, bar price coordination (NC Newsline)

health.label: Championed NC Medicaid expansion; platform: cap drug costs, protect ACA (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Vetoed 2019 bill requiring sheriffs to cooperate with ICE (WBTV)

climate.label: Launched NC Clean Energy Plan as governor (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Record: teacher raises, pre-K expansion, Teaching Fellows; opposed voucher expansion (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Long-standing opposition to NC voter ID legislation (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: As governor proposed $160M, 'the largest proposed housing investment in the state in over a decade': Housing Trust Fund, Workforce Housing Loan Program, affordable senior rentals (NLIHC)

taxes.label: Vetoed the GOP budget for keeping 'income tax breaks for corporations and families making over $200,000 a year instead of investing in education'; proposed freezing those cuts to raise teacher pay (NC Newsline)

safety.label: Vetoed HB 805, which imposed harsher penalties for rioting and tighter pretrial release rules (ACLU of North Carolina)

priorities: Lower health-care costs and expand Medicaid

candidates.name: Michael Whatley
candidates.background: Former Republican National Committee chairman and NC GOP chairman; earlier an energy-industry executive (Consumer Energy Alliance). Won the March 2026 Republican primary; endorsed by President Trump.

cost.label: Campaign: 'more money in your pockets,' fiscal responsibility, unleash American energy (campaign site)

immigration.label: '100% supportive' of securing the border and deportations (campaign site)

taxes.label: Campaign: fiscal responsibility, 'more money in your pockets', no detailed tax plan published (campaign site)

climate.label: Campaign: energy independence, 'unleashing American energy' (campaign site)

safety.label: Campaign: 'back the blue without apology,' restore law and order, opposes cashless bail (campaign site)

repro.label: Campaign pledges 'protecting life', no specifics published (campaign site)

democracy.label: Campaign: 'protect the ballot'; led election-integrity efforts as NC GOP chair (campaign site)

education.label: Pledges 'keeping radical woke ideology out of schools' (campaign site)

candidates.name: Don Davis
candidates.background: Don Davis is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina’s 1st District, a former Air Force officer, Presbyterian minister, ex-mayor of Snow Hill, and longtime state senator. He is widely described as a moderate Democrat with a notably bipartisan voting record, and faces a competitive 2026 rematch in a redrawn, more Republican-leaning district.
priorities: Make everyday life more affordable (groceries, health care)
Deliver for eastern NC, agriculture, rural water, flood recovery

candidates.name: Laurie Buckhout
candidates.now: Acting Asst. Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy
candidates.background: Laurie Buckhout is a retired U.S. Army colonel (26 years, Gulf War and Iraq) who founded a cyber/electronic-warfare consulting firm and served as Acting Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy in the Trump administration in 2025. She was the 2024 GOP nominee for this seat, losing to Davis by 1.6 points, and is Trump-endorsed for the 2026 rematch.
priorities: Lower cost of living and rein in spending
